newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian police seize suspicious Mexican plane.
newsitem.headline: Colombian police seize suspicious Mexican plane.

text.p: Colombian police were searching on Wednesday for five Mexicans who fled after their plane set down on a clandestine landing strip often used by drug traffickers, authorities said.

Mexican aviation authorities had reported the aircraft missing a short distance from the Caribbean coastal resort of Cancun on Tuesday evening. But the Colombian Air Force and police seized the plane, a twin-motor Superking-Beachcraft, after it landed later that night.
"The plane was intercepted and forced to land because of suspicious activities apparently related to drug-trafficking," a Colombian police spokesman told Reuters.
"The plane was seized after it landed on a clandestine landing strip, but the five occupants ran off and we're looking for them," he added.

Francisco Perez del Mazo -- first cousin of Alfredo del Mazo, the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) candidate for this year's Mexico City elections and former governor of the key State of Mexico -- was one of the passengers on board, Mexican aviation authorities said.
But a spokesman managing Alfredo del Mazo's campaign in the first direct elections for the Mexico City mayorship said he was "unaware" of any family ties between Perez del Mazo and the candidate.

The plane was seized near the town of Ayapel in Cordoba province, a lawless region of northwest Colombia where right-wing paramilitaries and leftist guerrillas have traditionally vied to control lucrative narcotics-smuggling and contraband routes.
The Mexican authorities said businessmen Eduardo Rous and Jose Lopez Castillo were listed as passengers on the flight, together with Perez del Mazo.

Alfredo del Mazo has held a number of senior government posts in Mexico. He narrowly lost to Carlos Salinas for the PRI party nomination in the 1988 presidential elections to succeed then president Miguel de la Madrid.
He was also seen as a close political ally of the Hank family, a dynasty of powerful Mexican businessmen, and Mexico's serving Interior Minister Emilio Chuayffet.
Mexico's ruling PRI party has been rocked by a series of allegations that senior members, including former president Salinas and his brother Raul, had close ties to drug traffickers.
